task.name: Semantic evaluation runs as an audit-only instrument, so its usefulness is measured before any readiness policy consumes it
task.story_text:
## What

A semantic evaluator that reads an issue for intent and emits structured findings or
`NO_FINDINGS`, as an audit-only instrument. It writes no labels, changes no admission answer,
and reports no readiness state. Its purpose in this slice is to be measured: to establish
whether machine semantic review recovers defects the structural gate cannot, before any
policy consumes its output.

Neither `NO_FINDINGS` nor `EVALUATION_FAILED` means ready. Naming a clean result after readiness would
give an unratified probabilistic outcome an authority this slice does not grant it.

## Why

Slice 6 of the typed intake contract (#2724), and the half the structural gate cannot cover.
The gate verifies required sections, vocabulary and diagnosis fields — all mechanical, all
passing on bodies that carry contract defects.

Observed repeatedly: on #2681 a single adversarial cross-model round surfaced four defects in
a body the gate returned `RUNNABLE` for — an unjustified dependency edge, a no-decision
default loose enough to permit the opposite of the gate's purpose, a gate anchored to a phase
stories routinely skip, and an example keyed to the wrong run identity. The same shape recurred
while filing this epic: #2408 satisfied the structural gate while its own criteria would have
made the closed verb vocabulary permanent. This issue's own earlier revision is a third
instance — it returned `RUNNABLE` while carrying an unnamed state distinction, an undefined
document revision, and no accept-case for a ratified finding.

This is not a gap the gate can close by adding rules. "The run takes a configured default
action" is structurally perfect and semantically open. Catching it requires reading for intent,
which is probabilistic.

The operator runs this by hand today, cross-model, with a hit rate high enough that it has
become habitual. That is the reason to build it — and also the reason to measure it first. The
readiness policy that consumes this output involves decisions that should be made against
evidence rather than in advance: which types require review, what a clean result entitles a
document to, and what an accepted finding does. Those land in the dependent slice, after this
one has produced data.

## Acceptance criteria

- The evaluator emits structured findings, `NO_FINDINGS`, or `EVALUATION_FAILED`, and changes
  nothing about the document it read. None of the three carries readiness authority.
- A run is identified by its evaluation input digest, its model id, and its prompt contract
  version. The digest covers the exact serialized input handed to the model — title, body, and
  the canonical type derived from the labels.
- Those three components are stored separately alongside the digest, so a later reader can tell
  which model and which contract version produced an outcome without recomputing it.
- A repeat run whose digest, model id and prompt contract version all match a recorded run
  returns that outcome without invoking a model. A change to any of the three re-runs.
- The evaluator runs only when a person invokes it, and no caller waits on its outcome.
- Every run writes a record carrying its outcome, its three identity components, its cost and
  its duration.
- The human baseline for a document is frozen before that document's evaluator output is
  revealed, so the comparison below is not contaminated by hindsight.
- Over a named corpus those records report: known-defect recovery, human-confirmed precision and
  the rejection rate, stability across repeat runs, cost per confirmed finding, and novel defects
  beyond the frozen baseline.
- `EVALUATION_FAILED` is written when no model is reached or the output does not parse, and no
  outcome enters the record for that run. A failed or absent run never reads as `NO_FINDINGS`.

## Example

From #2681 — a body the structural gate passed:

```
shape_check.check(...)          -> RUNNABLE
forge review-semantic 2681      -> 4 findings
  model=<id>  prompt=<version>  revision=<hash of title+body+labels>
  - dependency edge asserted with no justification
  - default action permits the opposite of the gate's purpose
  - criterion anchored to a phase stories routinely skip
  - example keyed to the wrong run identity

shape_check.check(...)          -> RUNNABLE   (unchanged — no admission effect)
```

Re-running against the same revision, model and prompt returns those four findings from the
record without invoking a model. Bumping the prompt version re-runs.

conventions_soft[0].value: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions

conventions_soft[1].value: Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

conventions_soft[2].value: Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.

conventions_soft[3].value: Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports

conventions_soft[4].value: Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

conventions_soft[5].value: When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it

conventions_soft[6].value: Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

conventions_soft[7].value: Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

claims.claim: For evidence-grounded advisory output, validating only citation identifiers is insufficient; acceptance needs to verify that the quoted evidence text itself matches the packet, or grounded-looking but unsupported claims can pass.

Advisory-only stages still need mechanical execution isolation before validation, because schema checks happen too late to mitigate risk if the agent is launched with normal checkout access and secrets.

When phase names are validated from a hand-maintained list instead of deriving from actual dispatch sites, the newest dispatched phase becomes unnameable in routing.phase_eligibility until a separate source edit adds it.

Fixing phase-vocabulary drift exposed a second coupling in knowledge-summary selection: preserving the plan-derived profile matters because fallback transport, budget, timeout, and role identity can be lost if agent-pool selection overrides it.
Guard tests against future phase drift are themselves prone to drift when they enumerate a fixed set of source files or apply incomplete literal-detection rules.
Validation messaging for operator-named phases must distinguish unrecognized phases from deliberately closed ones, or the loader can suggest a remediation it will not actually accept.
Helper APIs added during a registry refactor can remain disconnected unless call sites or tests are updated to exercise them directly.

correspondences.description: When an operator repeats review-semantic with --no-cache for an input digest, model id, and prompt contract version that already have a record, the command disables the cache path and the runner invokes the agent again.

The identity cache lookup returns the most recent record for a (digest, model id, prompt contract version) triple without filtering on status, so once a run fails to reach a model or fails to parse, every later default invocation for that identity is served the EVALUATION_FAILED record without invoking a model — and when a valid FINDINGS or NO_FINDINGS record was already stored for that same identity, the later failure record shadows it and is returned in its place.

The inherited-agent wait loop no longer defers its announcement past the first poll, so a story whose inherited group finishes inside one poll interval now emits a wait announcement it previously suppressed, and the change ships inside a semantic-evaluation story with no test asserting the new emission point.

When a frozen baseline already exists for a document digest, defect ids supplied on the invocation are discarded without any message, so an operator who passes a baseline that disagrees with the frozen one is told nothing and the store's own mismatch guard in freeze_baseline is never reached.
Two new top-level operator commands and their flags are registered without any entry in the CLI reference guide that the runbook names as the full flag reference.

With every same-identity repeat now served from the record store, two live records can no longer share an input digest, model id and prompt contract version through normal operator use, so the independent repeat stability counters stay at zero and the only stability the corpus report can show is cache replay, which is stable by construction.

handoff.summary: Implemented an audit-only semantic evaluation subsystem under `src/theforge/eval/` with separated input digesting, prompt construction, strict parsing, append-only record/baseline storage, manual runner orchestration, and corpus reporting. Wired new top-level CLI commands `review-semantic` and `semantic-report` through `eval_cmd.py` and `main.py`, enforced a derived read-only single-model invocation surface with fallbacks disabled, added focused regression coverage for digest identity, cache/rerun behavior, failure handling, baseline freezing, audit-only behavior, CLI output/dispatch, and corpus metrics, and fixed an existing inherited-agent wait logging race surfaced by the full-suite run.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The evaluator emits structured findings, `NO_FINDINGS`, or `EVALUATION_FAILED`, and changes nothing about the document it read. None of the three carries readiness authority.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Semantic parsing accepts only structured findings or `NO_FINDINGS`; launch/parse failures are recorded as `EVALUATION_FAILED`; the runner only loads issue title/body/labels and uses a derived read-only profile with no mutation tools, no fallback models, no API fallback, and no readiness-state integration.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A run is identified by its evaluation input digest, its model id, and its prompt contract version. The digest covers the exact serialized input handed to the model — title, body, and the canonical type derived from the labels.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The new input builder serializes canonical JSON over `title`, `body`, and `canonical_type` and hashes those exact bytes with SHA-256; records store `input_digest`, canonical `model_id`, and `prompt_contract_version` separately.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Those three components are stored separately alongside the digest, so a later reader can tell which model and which contract version produced an outcome without recomputing it.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Semantic review records in `.forge/audits/semantic-review/records.jsonl` store `input_digest`, `model_id`, and `prompt_contract_version` as independent fields, along with issue/type/cost/duration/cache metadata and optional resolved identity.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A repeat run whose digest, model id and prompt contract version all match a recorded run returns that outcome without invoking a model. A change to any of the three re-runs.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The manual runner serves exact-identity cache hits from the record store and appends a cache-hit record without calling `run_agent`; tests cover cache hits plus reruns on prompt-version, model-id, and digest changes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The evaluator runs only when a person invokes it, and no caller waits on its outcome.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Only the new manual CLI commands invoke the evaluator; no shape, groom, sprint, admission, or readiness path was wired to it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every run writes a record carrying its outcome, its three identity components, its cost and its duration.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Live runs and cache-served repeats both append records with identity, outcome/status, cost, duration, timestamps, and cache metadata; failed runs record `EVALUATION_FAILED` with failure detail and no parsed outcome payload.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The human baseline for a document is frozen before that document's evaluator output is revealed, so the comparison below is not contaminated by hindsight.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The runner refuses to reveal cached or live evaluator output until a frozen baseline exists for the input digest; `review-semantic` can create that baseline in the same invocation via `--baseline-defect-id` or `--freeze-empty-baseline`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Over a named corpus those records report: known-defect recovery, human-confirmed precision and the rejection rate, stability across repeat runs, cost per confirmed finding, and novel defects beyond the frozen baseline.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The new corpus loader/reporter computes those metrics from named corpus annotations plus stored records/baselines, distinguishes repeated identity groups, and excludes cost-unknown records from the spend metric while reporting the exclusion count.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `EVALUATION_FAILED` is written when no model is reached or the output does not parse, and no outcome enters the record for that run. A failed or absent run never reads as `NO_FINDINGS`.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Launch failures, unsuccessful/empty agent results, and parse failures are stored as `evaluation_failed` records with no `outcome`/`findings`; corpus reporting treats absent and failed runs separately and never maps them to `NO_FINDINGS`.

handoff.summary: This iteration fixes the semantic-eval identity cache contract without changing the audit-only design. Exact repeats now always reuse the recorded successful outcome for the same input digest, model id, and prompt contract version; transient `evaluation_failed` records remain append-only audit data but no longer satisfy cache lookups or shadow prior successful outcomes. The manual CLI no longer exposes a same-identity cache bypass, conflicting baseline defect ids now fail explicitly against an already frozen baseline, and focused regression coverage plus CLI reference docs were added.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When an operator repeats review-semantic with an input digest, model id, and prompt contract version that already have a record, the command must not bypass the exact-identity cache and invoke the agent again.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Removed the `--no-cache` CLI escape hatch and the runner now always consults the exact-identity cache before any model invocation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An `EVALUATION_FAILED` record must not poison or shadow the cached outcome for an identity; later default invocations should rerun if only failures exist, and should continue returning the latest successful outcome when one exists.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Identity lookup now filters to successful `findings`/`no_findings` records only, with regressions covering both failure-then-success and success-then-later-failure cases.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: P2 findings adjacent to the modified semantic-eval path should be fixed in scope.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Conflicting baseline defect ids against an already frozen digest now raise the store mismatch error instead of being ignored, and the CLI reference now documents `review-semantic` and `semantic-report`.

handoff.summary: Refined semantic corpus stability reporting without changing the audit-only design. The report now distinguishes measured stability from unmeasured repeat classes by emitting optional stability ratios and rendering cache-only repeat observations as `independent=unmeasured` instead of a misleading zero-denominator live-repeat count; added regression coverage for both measured live repeats and cache-only replay cases.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Combine those annotations with semantic_records to report known-defect recovery, human-confirmed precision, rejection rate, stability across repeated recorded outcomes, cost per confirmed finding, and confirmed novel defects not mapped to the frozen baseline; treat absent or failed records as failed/absent, never as NO_FINDINGS.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Stability reporting still uses the same recorded outcomes, but now marks independent live-repeat stability as unmeasured when only cache-derived repeats exist, avoiding a misleading 0/0 presentation while preserving the existing counters and cache-derived stability accounting.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Add focused regression tests for identity, cache, failure, audit-only behavior, CLI, and corpus metrics.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Added semantic report regressions covering both measured independent-repeat stability and the cache-only/unmeasured case, including rendered output. Verified with `make dev-check`.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 5 passes profile.model as model_id, but run_agent can use profile.fallback_models or a CLI-to-API fallback. AgentResult.model_used and transport_used record what actually served the invocation, and src/theforge/runners/cli.py explicitly notes that a bare model name is not a complete identity. The proposed records can therefore attribute and cache an outcome under a model that did not produce it.
  Suggestion: Define a canonical evaluation model identity including transport/provider, and use a dedicated single-model profile with fallbacks disabled so the pre-invocation cache key remains valid. Alternatively, store configured and resolved identities separately and specify cache behavior when they differ.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 3 and 5 reuse an arbitrary configured ModelProfile and its secrets/tool permissions. API profiles with allowed_tools enter an agent loop, while src/theforge/runners/runner_claude.py documents that an empty Claude CLI allowlist fails open to unrestricted tools. Thus the plan does not enforce its audit-only promise against issue edits or other mutations.
  Suggestion: Specify a mechanically non-mutating invocation surface: a tool-free stateless model call with only inference credentials, or an equivalent read-only profile that cannot invoke shell, GitHub mutation, or workspace-write tools. Add a test proving the derived dispatch profile has those capabilities removed.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The stated human-annotation risk is carried. Step 4 assumes frozen baseline defect IDs exist, while Step 5 only says to require or create a baseline and defines no CLI argument, separate command, or workflow for a human to supply and freeze those IDs before output is revealed. A later corpus annotation can be contaminated by evaluator output.
  Suggestion: Add an explicit baseline-capture/attestation path keyed by input_digest, require that immutable snapshot before cache lookup or model invocation is revealed, and make semantic-report consume the same snapshot.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] The stated stability risk is carried. Exact-identity repeats are always cache hits, so Step 4's proposed cache-hit consistency measures storage determinism and will be trivially stable; it cannot measure the probabilistic evaluator's stability. Step 6 also omits an independent-repeat stability test.
  Suggestion: Define a separate audit sampling mechanism that records independently invoked replicates without weakening normal cache semantics, then specify the finding-matching/agreement calculation and test it. If only cache-derived operational stability is intended, the acceptance criterion must be explicitly ratified to say that.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk #2 (stability underspecified). The cache AC guarantees an identity-exact repeat never re-invokes a model, so 'stability across repeat runs' can only be measured across records that differ in model id or prompt contract version, or via an explicit no-cache sampling path. Step 4 says it will report stability over recorded outcomes and flag it as cache-derived, but neither Step 3 nor Step 5 provides a way to produce more than one independent sample for a given identity, so the metric can be structurally degenerate (always 100% stable).
  Suggestion: Give the runner/CLI an explicit resample option (e.g. --no-cache / --repeat N) that appends an additional record for the same identity without serving from cache, and have semantic_report distinguish independent samples from cache-derived repeats in its output metadata.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] AgentResult.cost_usd is nullable across every transport (runner_claude.py:766/844/1159, runner_codex.py:859, runner_gemini.py:216 all return None on cost-unknown). Step 3 says 'records cost from AgentResult.cost_usd' without saying what a None cost writes, and Step 4's cost-per-confirmed-finding metric will divide by an incomplete cost total.
  Suggestion: Persist cost as nullable plus a provenance/cost-unknown marker in the record, and have semantic_report exclude cost-unknown records from cost-per-confirmed-finding while reporting how many were excluded rather than treating them as zero.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] shape_check.issue_spec.spec_for_labels (src/theforge/shape_check/issue_spec.py:620) returns None when no recognized type label is present or when more than one is. Step 1 derives canonical_type from it for the digest but does not define the serialized value in that case, which is a digest-stability concern since it lands in the hashed model input.
  Suggestion: Define an explicit canonical serialization for the None case (e.g. JSON null or a fixed 'untyped' token) in Step 1 and pin it with a digest test in Step 6.

finding_registry.description: When an operator repeats review-semantic with --no-cache for an input digest, model id, and prompt contract version that already have a record, the command disables the cache path and the runner invokes the agent again.

The identity cache lookup returns the most recent record for a (digest, model id, prompt contract version) triple without filtering on status, so once a run fails to reach a model or fails to parse, every later default invocation for that identity is served the EVALUATION_FAILED record without invoking a model — and when a valid FINDINGS or NO_FINDINGS record was already stored for that same identity, the later failure record shadows it and is returned in its place.

The inherited-agent wait loop no longer defers its announcement past the first poll, so a story whose inherited group finishes inside one poll interval now emits a wait announcement it previously suppressed, and the change ships inside a semantic-evaluation story with no test asserting the new emission point.

When a frozen baseline already exists for a document digest, defect ids supplied on the invocation are discarded without any message, so an operator who passes a baseline that disagrees with the frozen one is told nothing and the store's own mismatch guard in freeze_baseline is never reached.
Two new top-level operator commands and their flags are registered without any entry in the CLI reference guide that the runbook names as the full flag reference.

With every same-identity repeat now served from the record store, two live records can no longer share an input digest, model id and prompt contract version through normal operator use, so the independent repeat stability counters stay at zero and the only stability the corpus report can show is cache replay, which is stable by construction.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
